correctness.rationale: The normalized extension deficit is exactly the probabilistic deficit from the source. Permutation symmetry forces the tangent Hessian to be scalar. The source pair-merging identity reduces one tangent direction to the explicit H_s polynomial; differentiating at c=1/4 and summing the merged multiplicities yields the stated coefficient. Positivity follows from the s=2 term, and polynomial Taylor expansion gives the remainder. Exact-rational finite checks independently match the closed coefficient in several admissible cases but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The fresh sharp inequality identifies all maximizers but does not quantify near-extremizers. The exact isotropic Hessian is the natural first local stability invariant: it proves strict quadratic curvature in every modulus direction transverse to the extremizer manifold and gives that curvature in a closed finite-field occupancy formula. This is a structural refinement of the sharp endpoint theorem, not a routine parameter substitution.
